PROTECTING
SACRED SPACE
Decoding the Eccentric Flints of
the Classic Maya.

• The Artifact
Eccentrics are non-utilitarian artifacts
of chipped stone, featuring impossibly
delicate, undulating blades and
multi-headed silhouettes.
• The Mystery
For a century, their specific meaning
and function remained enigmatic to
scholars.
• The Tragedy of Context
Most known elaborate eccentrics were
looted. They have been scrubbed clean,
erasing crucial forensic data like paint,
wrappings, and the precise
archaeological context of their
deposition.

The Rosalila
Exception
In 1990, archaeologists at Copan,
Honduras, excavated a pristine cache
of 9 eccentrics and 3 bifaces.
A Pristine Dataset
Because the cache was excavated scientifically, the artifacts were left unwashed. They retained profound
forensic evidence-remnants of cinnabar paint and ancient textiles-proving these were not just carved
rocks, but carefully prepared ritual objects.

Entombed Alive: The Rosalila Structure
The Purpose
Built in the late 6th century AD to
celebrate Copan's dynasty founder,
K'inich Yax K'uk' Mo'
The Anomaly
Classic Maya tradition typically
dictated razing a building before
building its successor. Rosalila was
so esteemed it was painted white
and systematically entombed
intact.
The Cache Location
The 9 chert eccentrics were deliber-
ately cached deep within Rosalia's
interior. They were placed to protect
this hallowed space for eternity.

Piedra de Rayo: The Physics
of Fossilized Lightning
To the ancient Maya, chert and obsidian were not
merely rocks. Because striking these dense stones
produces hot sparks, and because lightning strikes on
silica-rich soil create glass fulgurites, the materials
were viewed as inherently powerful.
Chert and obsidian were believed to be created by
lightning striking the earth. They possessed an
inherent spiritual voltage. To shape an eccentric was
to wield fossilized lightning.

The Shape of a Strike
The Undulating Blade
The sharply recessed areas
and sinuous outlines are not
decorative flourishes.
In Mesoamerican art, the
undulating form is a universal
shorthand for a lightning bolt.
The Serpentine Connection
Lightning is frequently
depicted as a striking serpent
descending from the sky.
The Physical Blow
The deep indentations also
symbolically mimic violent
hammerstone blows-entirely
appropriate for a weapon
made of lightning.

Anatomy of a God's Weapon
The Blade
An undulating eccentric chert blade,
identical in shape to those found in
the Rosalila cache.
The Handle
A fire-breathing serpent, linking the
weapon to the sky and storms.
The Entity
The axe itself is often personified as
K'awiil, the Maya lightning deity. The
eccentrics at Copan literally incorporate
K'awiil heads into their chipped silhouettes.

A Masterclass in
Lithic Engineering
The Material Barrier
Normal nodular chert curves when flaked. To achieve
flat, massive eccentrics, the Copanec Maya had to
source rare tabular (flat slab) chert.
The Technique
Created via highly advanced indirect percussion and
pressure flaking, hollowing out impossible curves
without snapping the brittle stone.
Zero Use-Wear
Despite being shaped as axe heads and lances,
microscopic analysis shows no signs of physical
use. They were weapons engineered strictly for the
spirit realm.
